subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Container, timing, synchronization and dispatch primitives shared across startup, thread and network paths: SEH-managed singly-linked-list containers with 12-byte nodes, a high-resolution QueryPerformanceCounter timer object, mutex-gated state, guarded static-init scaffolding, and vtable-slot dispatch helpers for worker/trigger objects.

summary: This scope covers generic runtime infrastructure rather than domain gameplay. The strongest structural signal is a repeated singly-linked-list idiom: a 16-byte control block (head@+0x0, tail@+0x4, cursor@+0x8, count@+0xC) over 12-byte nodes (data@+0x0, next@+0x4, owns-data flag@+0x8), destroyed by a family of SEH-protected walkers that run a callback on flagged data before freeing it (0x00582FD0, 0x005833E0, 0x00585FB0, 0x00586240, 0x00586170), a variant that releases via the data object's vtable slot +4 (0x00583050), a block-releasing variant driven by NTimeCallbackLoopWithSEH (0x00583570), plus node removal (0x00583430) and node append (0x00586000). A second thread around a high-resolution timer object (float value@+0x0, QPC double base@+0x4) is evidenced by 0x00583660, 0x00583680 and 0x00583690 calling the QPC helpers 0x00568C60/0x00568CF0/0x00568D90. Synchronization appears as a mutex pair/list initializer (0x00585EA0), a 1 ms mutex flush/yield gate (0x005840D0, mutex at this+0xD4) and guarded OS-handle close slots inside a large complex object destroyed by 0x00583AE0 and whose node pool is managed by 0x00584130 (with the dual-list sub-object built by 0x00586320). Loose virtual dispatch helpers (0x005853B0, 0x00585400, 0x00585BF0) route work through fixed vtable slots; 0x00585BF0 is the only function whose owner the packet classifies DERIVED (TriggerDispatcher). Everything else in this packet carries an UNKNOWN owner, so every class here is a DERIVED/GUESS grouping justified by shared offsets, shared callees and shared control flow, never by proven identity.

function_roles.role: Destroy the linked list: for each node with the flag byte set, run SEHGuardedFunctionWithExceptionHandling on the node data, free the data when non-null, free the node, then clear head/tail/iterator/count and return 0.

Destroy the linked list: for each flagged node with non-null data, invoke the data object's virtual release at vtable+4 with argument 1, free the node via FreeWrapper_7bcf, under SEH handler 0x0059CE08, then zero head/tail/iterator/count.

Destroy the linked list (SEH-cleanup variant): free flagged node data via the SEH-guarded callback then FreeWrapper_7bcf, free every node, zero the container fields and return 0; called by 0x00583AE0.

Remove the first node whose data pointer matches the key; fix up head/tail/cursor/count, optionally clear the node flag, run the SEH-guarded cleanup on flagged data, free data and node; called by the network packet queue reader path.

Destroy the linked list (block-release variant): for each flagged node, run NTimeCallbackLoopWithSEH over the data block with entry size 4156, count read from block-4 and the EmptyStub_aa60 callback, then free block and node; zero the four container dwords.

Store the value parameter into the object's first dword and reset the high-precision timer sub-object at this+4 via TimerResetUsingQueryPerformanceCounter; called by timer-init and thread-resume paths.
Read the accumulated timer as float at this+0 plus the scaled QPC difference on the double at this+4; used by the mutex-guarded and thread-resume timer read paths.
Wrapper that forwards the object's timer-delta double member at this+4 to HighResolutionTimerDelta; called by the thread start path.
Constructor-style initializer that zero-fills a large object (explicit dwords/word/byte clears plus a 0xFC-byte memset at this+8) and returns this; called by 0x005837F0.

Counter helper: store two latched values into this+4/this+8, increment the counter at this+0, write it out through the output pointer and return it; called by the animation-timing update path 0x0057A5A0.

Complex object destructor: install destructor vtable 0x005B8B60, migrate a sub-object list, close and zero eight guarded OS handle slots, re-initialize a sub-object, destroy linked lists, clean up sub-object lists, then run a timed SEH-protected callback loop.
Mutex flush/yield gate: wait on the mutex handle at this+0xD4 with a 1 ms timeout and, on success, release it and return the release result; called by the thread start path 0x00583D90.

Search a node list for a node whose id matches a3, else take a node from the pool list (with pool reset on validation failure), set the node back-pointer, append it, record a3 at +0x410 and run the per-node step; invoked by 0x00585270.
Copy up to 16 characters from the source into the internal buffer at this+0x64 via the capped copy helper and force a null terminator at this+0x74; returns the source pointer.
Forwarding wrapper: copy the stack argument block into the object region at this+0x2C via ByteAlignedMemoryCopyWithOffset and return the callee pointer result; dispatched by 0x0057A4F0.
Asynchronous work-pipeline step: invoke vtable slot +0x3C, queue an APC, pop a node from a list, process it and hand it to vtable slot +0x5C; returns 0 when the pop fails; called by 0x0057A760.
Conditional dispatcher: on a successful bitmap-range occupancy test append via a list helper, otherwise route through vtable slot +0x2C, a processing helper and vtable slot +0x5C; always returns 1.
Single-field setter: store a2 into the object field at this+0x60 and return 1; dispatched by 0x0057A4F0.

Per-tick trigger dispatch: iterate a trigger collection through the object's vtable (slots +0xC8/+0x1C/+0xA4/+0xAC), build handler arguments from query and field helpers, invoke the handler table slot, release and end iteration; called by 0x0057A800.

Compiler-style guarded static-initialization wrapper: register an SEH frame from the handler table at 0x008D3E2C, run a one-time guard on the init counter and construct seven static objects linked into the parent exception frame.

Initialize a mutex-pair/list object: clear two pointer slots and two state flags, set two INFINITE timeouts, create two anonymous inheritable mutexes via CreateMutexA storing handles and created flags; returns this.
Clean up a linked list: per flagged node call the stub then free data when non-null, free every node, clear head/tail/iterator/count and return 0; called by 0x00583AE0.
Singly-linked list append: allocate a 12-byte node, store payload, zero next, set the flag byte, link as new tail, bump the count and return 1 (0 when the payload is null).
Teardown: close the owned handle at this+0x10 when the flag at this+0x18 is set, then walk-destroy the list with the SEH-guarded data cleanup and zero the list fields.
Destroy a linked list under SEH record 0x0059D138: per flagged node call the stub then free data, free every node, zero the four list-management fields and return 0.

Build two intrusive linked lists over a 2100-byte buffer: allocate a wrapper and the buffer, run NTimeCallbackLoopWithSEH_a6eb with the buffer init callback, link one flagged node into list 1 and two nodes into list 2; called once by 0x00584130.

classes.name: SinglyLinkedListNode
classes.responsibility: 12-byte node element used by the list containers in this scope: payload pointer, next link and an owns-data flag byte that selects SEH-guarded cleanup.

classes.name: SinglyLinkedList
classes.responsibility: SEH-managed singly-linked list: 16-byte control block (head/tail/cursor/count) over 12-byte nodes; destruction walks free flagged node data under an exception guard before releasing nodes.

classes.name: HandleGuardedList
classes.responsibility: List container extended with a guarded OS handle at +0x10 (validity flag at +0x18) that is closed before the list is destroyed.

classes.name: MutexProtectedList
classes.responsibility: Object pairing two anonymous mutexes (handles at +0xC/+0x1C, created flags at +0x14/+0x24, INFINITE timeouts at +0x10/+0x20) with two list/pointer slots and state flags, initialized by 0x00585EA0.

classes.name: DoubleListBuffer
classes.responsibility: Sub-object holding two intrusive linked lists (list 1 at +0x0..+0xC, list 2 at +0x10..+0x1C) built over a 2100-byte buffer initialized through the timed callback loop; 0x00586320 is its constructor and the pool lists used by ComplexResourceObject at parent+0xFC.

classes.name: ComplexResourceObject
classes.responsibility: Large multi-sub-object resource owner: eight guarded OS handle slots (each with a paired validity flag), a node-pool list and sub-object list with iterators, a destructor that migrates/closes/cleans everything (0x00583AE0) and a node search-or-allocate path (0x00584130).

classes.name: HiResTimer
classes.responsibility: High-resolution timer object: float value/accumulator at +0x0 and a QPC-based double base at +0x4, manipulated through the QPC helpers 0x00568C60/0x00568CF0/0x00568D90.

classes.name: WorkerMutexGate
classes.responsibility: Mutex flush/yield gate: waits on a mutex handle at this+0xD4 with a 1 ms timeout and releases when acquired; used by the thread start path.

classes.name: AsyncWorkItem
classes.responsibility: Asynchronous worker step that dispatches through vtable slot +0x3C, queues an APC, pops a node from a list, processes it and hands it to vtable slot +0x5C.

classes.name: BitmapSlotRouter
classes.responsibility: Conditional dispatcher that appends on a successful bitmap-range occupancy test or routes through vtable slots +0x2C and +0x5C otherwise.

classes.name: TriggerDispatcher
classes.responsibility: Per-tick trigger iteration and handler dispatch over a collection reached through the object's vtable (begin/current/count/predicate/release/end slots); the only owner in this scope the packet classifies DERIVED.

classes.name: VirtualDispatchOperationHandler
classes.responsibility: Dispatched virtual operations on a common object, both invoked by VirtualFunctionDispatchWithStackFrames: copy the stack argument block into +0x2C, or store a scalar into +0x60.

classes.name: NameBufferHolder
classes.responsibility: Object with an internal 16-byte name buffer at +0x64 (null terminator forced at +0x74) filled through the capped copy helper.

classes.name: CounterLatchState
classes.responsibility: Small counter object holding a counter at +0x0 and two latched values at +0x4/+0x8, updated by the animation-timing helper 0x005836E0.

classes.name: LargeInitializedState
classes.responsibility: Large object whose constructor-style initializer zero-fills a set of scattered fields and a 0xFC-byte block; the fields' semantic roles are not established in this scope.

classes.name: GuardedStaticInitScope
classes.responsibility: Compiler-style guarded one-time static-initialization scaffolding: SEH frame setup, a one-time guard on a global init counter, and construction of seven static objects linked into the parent exception frame.

transitions.trigger: LinkedListNodeAppend_6000 links the first node and sets head/tail/cursor
destroy/cleanup walk or node removal clears head and count to zero
CreateMutexA returns a non-null handle; the created flag at +0x14/+0x24 is set to 1

interfaces.name: IListContainerOps
interfaces.purpose: Common singly-linked-list container operations over the 16-byte head/tail/cursor/count control block: append, remove-by-key, and SEH-protected destruction with per-node data cleanup.

interfaces.name: IVTableDispatchSink
interfaces.purpose: Object that routes work through fixed vtable slots; the concrete slot semantics are object-type dependent and are not resolvable from this scope.

interfaces.name: IHighResolutionTimerSource
interfaces.purpose: High-resolution timer source backed by QPC scaling, exposing store-and-reset, accumulated read and delta update operations on a shared timer object.

dependencies.to: Data object virtual release at vtable+4
Timed SEH callback loop and single-function wrapper
Buffer init loop (0x0058A6EB) and node allocator (0x00587C03)
Bitmap occupancy, list append and processing helpers (0x00586D00 / 0x00584DD0 / 0x00584230)
APC queue, list pop and value processing helpers (0x00585DE0 / 0x00584E30 / 0x00586E50)

compatibility_contracts.name: SinglyLinkedListNodeLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: Replacement code that owns these lists must preserve the 12-byte node layout: payload pointer at +0x0, next pointer at +0x4, owns-data flag byte at +0x8; flagged nodes have their data released through the SEH-guarded callback before the node is freed.

compatibility_contracts.name: ListContainerControlBlock
compatibility_contracts.description: The list container control block is four dwords at base+0x0 (head), +0x4 (tail), +0x8 (cursor) and +0xC (count); destroy paths clear all four after the walk and append/remove update them.

compatibility_contracts.name: OSHandleLifecycle
compatibility_contracts.description: Handles are created through CreateMutexA (0x0059E1AC), waited on through WaitForSingleObject (0x0059E1A0), released through ReleaseMutex (0x0059E1A4) and closed through CloseHandle (0x0059E1A8); guarded handle slots pair the handle with a validity byte that gates closing.

compatibility_contracts.name: SEHRegisteredFrames
compatibility_contracts.description: Several container and init functions register SEH frames whose handler records are the globals 0x0059CDE8, 0x0059CE08, 0x0059D046, 0x0059D138, 0x0059D166 and 0x00583AA0; a replacement must keep the destruction/cleanup exception-safe against the same failure points.

compatibility_contracts.name: HiResTimerQPCBase
compatibility_contracts.description: The timer object stores a float value at +0x0 and a double QPC base at +0x4; accumulated reads add the scaled QPC difference to the float and resets re-arm the base through the 0x00568C60/0x00568CF0/0x00568D90 helpers.

unresolved: Almost every owner in this packet is UNKNOWN; every class here is a DERIVED/GUESS grouping justified by shared offsets, shared callees and shared control flow. Equal offsets on different bases are structural parallels, not proven identity.

this+0xD4 is read as a mutex handle by 0x005840D0 and closed as a guarded handle slot by 0x00583AE0's destructor; the two functions may share an owner but the packet does not prove common ownership, so they are modeled as separate classes.

The 16-byte list control layout (head/tail/cursor/count) recurs in SinglyLinkedList, HandleGuardedList, MutexProtectedList and DoubleListBuffer at overlapping offsets; the packet proves each function walks the same node idiom but not that the containing classes are identical.
The vtable slot semantics at obj+0x1C/0x20/0x2C/0x3C/0x5C/0xA4/0xAC/0xC8/0xCC and the data-object vtable+4 release are object-type dependent and unresolved.
The node field at +0xC is recorded by the corpus but has no direct access in the raw sources of this scope; it is modeled as UNKNOWN metadata/padding.
The double at HiResTimer+0x4 has no packet field evidence reference, only raw source text; whether the float at +0x0 is a running accumulator or a fixed offset is unproven.
The 0xFC-byte memset block in 0x005836A0 overlaps the explicitly cleared fields; the relationship between the memset region and the fields at 0x11C/0x11E/0x120 is not established.

0x00586320's list offsets (+0x0..+0x1C) are relative to the sub-object at parent+0xFC, not to the parent base; the embedding of DoubleListBuffer inside ComplexResourceObject is inferred from 0x00584130 calling 0x00586320 with this+63.
Three write-only globals 0xFF00000000005450/0xFF00000000005451/0xFF00000000005452 appear in the 0x00585EA0 packet with write access but never in the decompiled source; their purpose is unexplained.
The guarded static-init helpers sub_59A54D and sub_59A5E9 and the seven constructed static objects in 0x00585E50 are opaque at this scope.
The count passed to NTimeCallbackLoopWithSEH by 0x00583570 is read from the 4 bytes preceding the data block base; that offset is not in the packet field evidence.
0x00583050's argument 1 to the vtable+4 call and the exact semantics of the node flag byte and SEH cleanup callback are defined by the data owner, not by these list functions.
The list append count dword at +0xC is classified read in the packet field table although 0x00586000 increments it; the classification may predate the write.

Callers outside this scope (0x0057A4F0, 0x0057A5A0, 0x0057A760, 0x0057A800, 0x005835F0, 0x005837F0, 0x00583D90, 0x00584F90, 0x00585270, 0x00585680) are referenced by evidence only; their object ownership is not resolved here.
